papers.title: Self-Supervised Visual On-Policy Distillation

summary.tldr: Self-Supervised Visual On-Policy Distillation (S^2VOPD) creates an informative teacher-student asymmetry without privileged labels or stronger models by distilling an unaugmented visual distribution into a strongly augmented student view.
key_points: S^2VOPD distills the teacher distribution conditioned on the original image on-policy into the student distribution conditioned on a strongly augmented view.
Symmetric self-distillation degrades performance, whereas asymmetric augmentations improve it up to a peak at moderate strength.
Augmentations must remain task-consistent, as completely removing question-relevant evidence induces uninformative discrepancies.
S^2VOPD increases Qwen3.5-4B accuracy from 70.7% to 77.4% across six fine-grained perception benchmarks, outperforming Qwen3-VL (235B) and GPT-5.4.
The method recovers 96% of the performance gains of privileged-information distillation methods using the same training data.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables state-of-the-art visual reasoning capabilities in smaller vision-language models without requiring ground-truth annotations, human reward signals, or larger teacher models.

papers.title: VibeWorlding: Can Multimodal Agents Construct 3D Open Worlds End-to-End?

summary.tldr: VibeWorlding introduces a framework, benchmark, sandbox environment, and multimodal RL-trained models to evaluate and improve end-to-end 3D open world construction by multimodal agents.
key_points: VWE-BENCH includes 2,616 3D assets, 323 human-annotated seed 3D worlds, and 6,828 reverse-synthesized user queries.
VibeWorlding-Gym provides a joint multimodal RL training framework with a Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool sandbox and a rubric-based verifier assessing intent fulfillment and physical feasibility.
Frontier models like GPT-5.5 and Qwen3.8-Max achieve under 60% success on the task, identifying precise 3D world editing as the primary performance bottleneck.
RL post-training enables open-source models to excel, with VibeWorlder-8B matching frontier MLLMs and VibeWorlder-30B-A3B achieving the highest overall Pass@1 score.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that targeted reinforcement learning post-training can allow open-source MLLMs to outperform leading proprietary models in complex 3D tool use and spatial world generation.

papers.title: HarnessEval-W: Agentifying the Evaluation of Visual Worlds

summary.tldr: HarnessEval-W is an agentified evaluation pipeline for visual world models that replaces scalar metrics with a transparent, verifiable evidence tree generated by specialized sub-agents.
key_points: Decomposes complex evaluation cases into subproblems handled by specialized sub-agents equipped with context-tailored diagnostic tools.
Employs a parent agent to aggregate and validate sub-agent evidence, producing a final verdict backed by an explicit reasoning chain.
Evaluated across 18 world models over 330 evaluation cases, demonstrating high alignment with human preferences in visual, physical, and causal rollout assessments.
Open-sourced as a live benchmark designed to expand with new diagnostic skills and test cases as world models evolve.
summary.why_it_matters: It replaces opaque, brute-force scalar metrics with interpretable and verifiable reasoning chains to accurately assess physics and causality in world model rollouts.

papers.title: ClawGym II: Exploring Black-Box RL on Agent Harness

summary.tldr: ClawGym II introduces a unified black-box RL framework using sandbox execution infrastructure and proxy-intercepted trajectory prefix trees to train agents like Qwen3-30A3B through complex, heterogeneous harnesses.
key_points: Decouples policy optimization from opaque harness execution by placing a serving proxy at the model boundary to capture calls.
Reconstructs multi-turn trajectories into prefix trees to optimize adapted PPO (critic-based) and GRPO (critic-free) algorithms while maintaining training-inference consistency.
Utilizes a sandbox-based execution infrastructure for isolated, large-scale concurrent rollouts and supports mix-harness training across heterogeneous systems.
Achieved Pass@1 improvements on ClawGym-Bench using Qwen3-30A3B by 9.98 points via OpenClaw and 14.81 points via Claude Code, maintaining stability over 200-400 steps.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables stable, scalable reinforcement learning for LLM agents operating within complex, black-box execution harnesses on long-horizon tasks.

papers.title: SimpleOPD: Simple Tokenizer-Agnostic On-Policy Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning

summary.tldr: SimpleOPD enables tokenizer-agnostic on-policy distillation from long-context teacher models to short-context students using shared text-space token alignment and constrained reference KL loss.
key_points: Aligns student and teacher tokens by mapping them to identical text spans within a shared text space to resolve tokenizer mismatches.
Introduces a student reference KL loss and masks the advantages of special termination tokens (like end-of-text markers) to control response length explosion and policy drift.
Distills proof-reasoning capabilities from the SU-01 long-context model into diverse short-context student models (Qwen3, Qwen3.5, Intern-S2, GLM-4.7, Gemma-4).
Intern-S2-Preview achieved a 21.2-point improvement on ProofBench, reaching a score of 55.2 and outperforming Gemini-2.5-Pro, while also improving on general science benchmarks HLE and HiPhO.
summary.why_it_matters: It allows smaller, short-context open-weights models to efficiently acquire advanced long-form reasoning capabilities from specialized teachers without requiring identical tokenizers.

papers.title: UI-Mate: Advancing Open-Weight Foundation GUI Agents with In-Context Demonstrations

summary.tldr: UI-Mate is an open-weight 27B GUI foundation agent trained with an environment-grounded stack and in-context demonstration learning, setting new open-weight state-of-the-art performance on OSWorld-Verified and WindowsAgentArena.
key_points: Integrates a closed-loop training data engine automating generation, rollout, filtering, SFT, and online RL in parallel environments using task-verifier bundles.
Utilizes in-context demonstration learning to parse multimodal demonstrations into subtask workflows, follow relevant steps, and dynamically re-plan from live UI states.
Introduces OSWorkerBench, a benchmark of 100 long-horizon office tasks across 41 applications, featuring self-demo (33 tasks) and variant-demo (45 tasks) evaluation settings.
UI-Mate-27B achieves 77.0% on OSWorld-Verified, 66.2% on WindowsAgentArena, and 41.0% strict success on OSWorkerBench (a 17.7-point improvement over its Qwen3.6-27B base).
A single demonstration on OSWorkerBench's self-demo subset increased strict task success from 17.2% to 35.4% and progress from 67.9% to 81.1%.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that combining in-context multimodal demonstrations with online RL substantially improves the execution reliability of open-weight models during long-horizon desktop automation tasks.

papers.title: DFM Mimir v1: An Open HRM Delivering Frontier Performance at 1B Parameters Using Only Permissible Post-Training Data

summary.tldr: Mimir v1 is an open 1-billion-parameter Hierarchical Reasoning Model trained from scratch using only permissible post-training data across 161 datasets.
key_points: Based on the Hierarchical Reasoning Model (HRM) architecture and trained entirely from scratch.
Utilizes a post-training data mixture comprising 161 permissible datasets.
Outperforms the baseline HRM-Text 1B model across 20 English, Math & Code, and Danish benchmarks.
Competes directly with larger frontier models, including Qwen 3.5 4B and Gemma 4 E2B, while setting a new state of the art for Danish language performance.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that competitive frontier performance in smaller language models can be achieved using strictly ethically sourced and permissible datasets.

papers.title: Agentic Transaction: Towards ACID-Compliant Agent Systems

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced the concept of agentic transactions, framing LLM agent execution around an ACID-compliant framework featuring four semantic guarantees to improve reliability in dynamic workflows.
key_points: Reinterprets classical ACID properties into Semantic Atomicity, Semantic Consistency, Semantic Isolation, and Semantic Durability for autonomous LLM systems.
Implements guarantees via transactional exploration-execution-validation cycles, transactional skill hubs, semantic dependency-aware isolation, and transaction-aware state management.
Uses confidence divergence-based validation to maintain execution consistency despite model uncertainty.
Outperforms state-of-the-art agents, including Claude Code, by 10.6% on widely used benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: Adapting database transactional guarantees to agent architectures provides a principled mechanism for reliable, safe, and durable long-horizon task execution.

papers.title: GenRouter: Unified Workflow Routing for Agentic Image Generation

summary.tldr: GenRouter is the first unified workflow routing framework for agentic image generation, dynamically routing prompts to optimal workflow topologies to improve visual alignment while cutting compute costs by over 95%.
key_points: Standardizes diverse agentic pipelines into universal primitives and templates via GenCanvas.
Routes prompts dynamically using demand profiling, experience matching, and Pareto filtering.
Reduces execution costs by over 95% and latency by 65% compared to heavyweight static pipelines.
Self-evolves through accumulated experience, enabling zero-shot generalization that doubles efficiency.
summary.why_it_matters: It prevents compute-mismatch in agentic image generation by dynamically matching prompt complexity to the necessary workflow, drastically reducing operational latency and cost.

papers.title: An Empirical Study of Training Pixel-Space Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

summary.tldr: Researchers established a latent-to-pixel training strategy that overcomes slow pixel-space pre-training, enabling pixel-space text-to-image diffusion models to match or exceed latent-space performance while achieving up to 4.75x inference speedups.
key_points: Identified that direct, large-scale pre-training of text-to-image diffusion models in pixel space converges significantly slower than in latent space.
Proposed a latent-to-pixel training recipe that learns generative priors in latent space before transitioning to pixel space during post-training.
Evaluated crucial transition design choices: weight initialization, data composition, prediction targets, decoder architectures, and noise schedules.
Demonstrated 3.18x to 4.75x end-to-end inference speedups over latent-space models without sacrificing generation quality.
summary.why_it_matters: This recipe eliminates the efficiency trade-off of pixel-space diffusion models, delivering significantly faster end-to-end image generation without compromising output quality.

papers.title: MegaParts: Scaling Part-Aware 3D Object Generation to 300 Parts via Token-Efficient Autoregressive Modeling

summary.tldr: MegaParts is an autoregressive 3D generation framework using a token-efficient vector-quantized shape tokenizer to scale part-aware generation up to 300 parts and 256k-token sequence lengths.
key_points: Employs a vector-quantized shape tokenizer that learns discrete latent representations for part geometry using adaptive-length tokenization based on part complexity.
Trains a large language model on a unified structured sequence containing object bounding boxes, part bounding boxes, and part shape tokens.
Scales part-aware 3D object generation up to 300 parts and context lengths up to 256k tokens using an efficient long-context training strategy.
Outperforms baseline autoregressive and diffusion models in generated mesh quality and geometric fidelity.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that token-efficient autoregressive modeling can replace diffusion models for high-fidelity 3D object generation requiring complex, fine-grained part assemblies.

papers.title: Understanding Cognition-Induced Risks in Agentic AI Systems

summary.tldr: A new framework categorizes cognition-induced risks in LLM-powered agentic AI systems across physical, social, and self-referential levels to analyze threats to human agency, autonomy, and control.
key_points: Evaluates frontier LLM agentic systems through a three-level cognitive scope framework: physical cognition, social cognition, and self-referential cognition.
Maps specific cognitive levels to corresponding risks regarding human agency, autonomy, and system control capabilities.
Proposes targeted mitigation strategies designed to enhance system controllability and support long-term safe development.
summary.why_it_matters: Systematically categorizing how expanding AI cognitive capabilities threaten human control provides a structured foundation for designing actionable safety guardrails in autonomous agentic systems.

papers.title: R^3-Bench: LLMs Struggle with Resource-Rational Reasoning under Shared Budgets

summary.tldr: R^3-Bench introduces a benchmark to evaluate LLMs on resource-rational reasoning under shared computational budgets across math, programming, and abstract reasoning in tool-free and agentic environments.
key_points: Evaluates six-problem suites under shared budgets against an offline empirical oracle derived from matched single-problem response curves.
Across 72 evaluation cells covering six models, the oracle performance matched or exceeded the model's actual contest performance in all cells and was strictly higher in 71.
Equal-allocation replay outperformed contest results for four of six models under moderate tool-free budget pressure.
In agentic settings under high budget pressure, fixed resource schedulers beat contest means in six of nine cells, but no single scheduler policy proved optimal across all domains.
Trajectory diagnostics show models fail to update strategies dynamically under budget constraints.
summary.why_it_matters: Current LLMs suffer from a gap between their baseline problem-solving competence and their ability to dynamically allocate compute under global budget constraints.

papers.title: Ventor-QTest: Threat-Model-Driven Verification of Vendor-Hosted LLM APIs

summary.tldr: Ventor-QTest is a black-box audit tool that evaluates vendor-hosted LLM API fidelity using repeated requests and long-sequence probes without requiring logprob access.
key_points: Formalizes hosted model routing as a stochastic process and introduces two metrics: Average Fidelity Loss (AFL) and Extreme Fidelity Loss (EFL).
AFL measures output distribution discrepancies via a null-bias-corrected, within-window mean coarsened-KL statistic from repeated frozen-context requests.
EFL evaluates empirical upper-tail run-level reference-centered surprisal across independent long-sequence runs.
AFL correlates strongly with logprob-derived comparators, while pronounced EFL aligns with reduced Terminal-Bench pass rates in long-horizon tasks.
Neither AFL nor EFL shows a strong route-level association with short-form GPQA-Diamond accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables model consumers to audit third-party API quality and detect silent performance degradation in long-horizon agentic workflows without relying on vendor-provided log probabilities.

papers.title: VideoGAIA: A Benchmark for General AI Assistants on Agentic Video Understanding

summary.tldr: VideoGAIA is a new benchmark featuring 271 model-human co-designed tasks that evaluates multimodal models on multi-turn, tool-augmented agentic video understanding.
key_points: Formulates video understanding as a multi-turn, tool-augmented process requiring iterative perception, tool invocation, and multimodal evidence integration.
Contains 271 human-verified task instances designed to replace saturated single-turn benchmarks like Video-MME.
Frontier models, including GPT-5.5 and Kimi-K3, achieve under 60% accuracy on the benchmark.
summary.why_it_matters: It establishes a harder, tool-use-focused benchmark to drive the evolution of multimodal LLMs from static video question answering to dynamic, agentic interaction.

papers.title: Would this change your answer? Evaluating Explanations of LLM Behavior In The Wild with Counterfactual Experiments

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced CHIVE, an agentic pipeline that discovers naturally-occurring LLM behaviors and generates explanations evaluated through counterfactual prompt edits.
key_points: Introduced CHIVE (Counterfactual Hypothesis Investigation Via Edits) to identify unexpected model behaviors and investigate them via counterfactual prompt edits.
Evaluated common LLM interpretability techniques using counterfactual simulatability and found they provided no uplift in predicting counterfactual model behaviors.
Used CHIVE-generated counterfactual experiment data to train models, demonstrating that outcome-prediction capability generalizes to out-of-distribution settings.
summary.why_it_matters: CHIVE provides an automated framework to rigorously evaluate interpretability techniques and produce training data that improves counterfactual reasoning about LLM behavior.

papers.title: Le Critique: Privileged Value Functions for LLM Reinforcement Learning

summary.tldr: Le Critique introduces Privileged Value Functions (PVF) and the TETHER baseline to enhance token-level credit assignment and performance in LLM reinforcement learning over standard value functions and GRPO.
key_points: Privileged Value Functions (PVF) inject additional task-relevant, token-level signals into the value function without introducing bias into the policy objective.
TETHER is an adaptive baseline method that interpolates between group-relative and value-function baselines based on the current accuracy of the value function.
The proposed methods address drawbacks of group-relative algorithms like GRPO, such as sequence-level-only credit, training bottlenecks from straggler rollouts, and off-policyness.

Evaluations across reasoning tasks demonstrate that PVF and TETHER consistently outperform standard value function baselines and achieve competitive or superior performance compared to mean-baseline GRPO.
summary.why_it_matters: The approach makes learned value functions more practical and performant for LLM training, offering fine-grained token-level credit assignment without relying on large rollout groups.

papers.title: Does the LM Head Create a Harmful Gradient Bottleneck? A Causal Test

summary.tldr: A backward-only intervention study isolates LM-head gradient rank reduction, showing that while gradient compression exists, it is far less harmful than forward-pass factorized projections and does not constitute a primary optimization bottleneck.
key_points: Tested a backward-only intervention that reduces gradient rank sent to the Transformer while keeping ordinary logits and parameter updates unchanged.
At half rank in a BPE-8192 model, backward-only rank reduction increased loss by 0.0586, whereas an equally ranked factorized forward head increased loss by 0.1795.
Removing the vocabulary-space residual's contribution to the standard LM-head update proved harmful to training.
Tested auxiliary feedback routes failed to outperform tuned backpropagation.
Controls showed projection diagnostics fail to reliably predict training progress and adding never-target output classes does not impair learning.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that geometric compression in the LM head does not severely bottleneck optimization, indicating that architectural modifications targeting gradient rank projection yield minimal optimization benefits.

papers.title: HalluTracer: Hallucination Detection via Depth-Averaging Truth Signals

summary.tldr: HalluTracer is a white-box detection framework that aggregates weakly correlated truthfulness signals across all network layers during the forward pass using depth averaging to reduce noise.
key_points: Identifies that internal truthfulness signals across different layers are weakly correlated, enabling noise reduction via simple depth averaging.
Aggregates truthfulness evidence across every forward-pass layer before the language model emits an answer token.
Transforms hallucination detection from a layer-selection paradigm into a full-depth aggregation approach.
Outperforms matched white-box baselines by 1 to 14 points across six open-source language models and five benchmark datasets.
summary.why_it_matters: By capturing truthfulness signals distributed across the entire model depth rather than relying on single-layer probes, developers can build more reliable hallucination detectors for high-stakes LLM deployments.

papers.title: Step-Level On-Policy Distillation: Interpolating Between On-Policy Distillation and Supervised Fine-Tuning

summary.tldr: Step-Level On-Policy Distillation (SOPD) provides step-level teacher supervision on student-generated trajectories to interpolate between the long-horizon corrections of SFT and the state-alignment advantages of OPD.
key_points: Standard token-level On-Policy Distillation (OPD) offers fragmented corrections that fail to unfold complete repair paths along erroneous trajectories.
SOPD provides step-level supervision conditioned on student-visited states, mathematically reducing to SFT or approximating OPD at different step-length limits.

Demonstrates substantial performance gains over conventional SFT and Vanilla OPD across reasoning and agent domains, including a 13.4 percentage point success rate improvement on ALFWorld over Vanilla OPD.
summary.why_it_matters: SOPD provides a superior distillation framework for reasoning and agent tasks by combining long-horizon path corrections with on-policy state alignment.

papers.title: Prior Audit-Repair Context Shifts LLM Verifier Thresholds Toward Leniency

summary.tldr: Including a completed audit-repair episode in an LLM verifier's context systematically shifts its decision threshold toward leniency, reducing false alarm rates on subsequent tasks by 2.8 to 11.5 percentage points.
key_points: Evaluations on human-verified-correct ProcessBench traces showed a 9% to 25% relative reduction in false alarms across 15 of 15 model and wording combinations compared to a length-matched control.

Signal-detection analysis indicates the shift occurs in the decision criterion threshold (statistically significant in 13 of 15 cases) rather than in discrimination ability (d' showed no significant change).
Prior audit episodes containing flagged errors reduced false alarms even further, contradicting predictions from accumulated-message negativity asymmetry literature.
The threshold shift toward leniency persisted at similar relative scales when reasoning was enabled, and a manual audit showed 82% of baseline false alarms were simply incorrect errors.
Decomposition reveals that the effect is driven by complementary components: repair content and audit verdicts carry different weights depending on the model family.
summary.why_it_matters: Wiring LLM checkers and fixers sequentially alters the checker's baseline severity threshold, meaning verifier accuracy and strictness depend heavily on prior in-context interaction history.

papers.title: From Sequence to Structure: Relational Uncertainty Propagation for LLM Agents

summary.tldr: RUPA is a trajectory-level uncertainty quantification framework for LLM agents that models execution histories as directed dependency graphs to propagate risk across long-range reasoning steps, tool interactions, and environment feedback.
key_points: Constructs a directed trajectory graph where reasoning states, tool interactions, and environment feedback serve as nodes linked by temporal and semantic dependency edges.
Propagates uncertainty over the trajectory graph to model error accumulation and transfer across multi-step agent histories.
Combines propagated graph signals with trajectory-level behavioral features and goal-alignment metrics to calculate final confidence estimates.
Evaluated across six open-source LLMs on the tau-2, Terminal-Bench-2, and GAIA benchmarks, demonstrating improved failure detection and execution accuracy over local UQ methods.
summary.why_it_matters: By accounting for long-range dependency chains rather than isolated step probabilities, RUPA enables earlier detection of agent failures and improves execution reliability in complex, long-horizon tasks.

papers.title: Aborted but Not Forgotten: KV-Cache Retention Breaks Rollback Consistency in Language Agents

summary.tldr: Researchers identify a state integrity failure where language agents retaining KV-cache state attend to logically aborted transcript branches, breaking rollback consistency even when the served prompt text is clean.
key_points: Logical transcript rollbacks fail to clear retained KV-cache states, creating a cross-layer gap where models attend to content discarded by the application.
A same-token/different-cache audit across seven open-weight model families (3.8B-36B) showed stale KV state alone flipped decisions in 25 of 63 tested cells.
The vulnerability reproduces in real-world setups including default Hugging Face Transformers cache-reuse paths and LangGraph time-travel implementations.
Rebuilding the cache or implementing transaction-local cache restoration completely closes the channel without requiring a global cache flush.
summary.why_it_matters: Applications relying on agentic rollback or time-travel mechanisms remain vulnerable to prompt injection or state corruption unless the underlying KV-cache is explicitly restored alongside the text transcript.

papers.title: Towards Computational Provenance: Carrying Causal-State Evidence in Generated Text

summary.tldr: A controlled study demonstrates that neural models can embed detectable, verified causal-state evidence into subtle statistical patterns of generated text without altering the final output answer.
key_points: Evaluated on both modular feed-forward networks and transformer architectures trained on arithmetic tasks with two discrete intermediate states.
Internal states were authenticated and used to modulate text statistical patterns without changing the final computational answer.
Achieved successful detection across all 128 matched pairs in public and sealed protected evaluations for both feed-forward and transformer systems.

Causal computation reproduced across five independently trained feed-forward models and three transformers, while linear probes failed to recover naturally learned intermediate states in an answer-only baseline.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a proof of concept for establishing computational provenance, enabling third parties to verify which internal neural pathways were executed to produce a model's output.

papers.title: What Do Compliance Detectors Read? An Audit of Activation Probes and Guard Models

summary.tldr: Researchers identify "rule blindness" in compliance detectors and activation probes, showing their verdicts rely on scenario surface features rather than governing rules, and propose the training-free Internal Compliance Score (ICS) for efficient auditing.
key_points: Tested compliance detectors and activation probes suffer from rule blindness, maintaining unchanged accuracy when governing rules are deleted, permuted, or substituted.
A policy-conditioned guard correctly cited governing clauses but barely altered its verdict when a clause was swapped with its permissive counterpart.
A purpose-built benchmark crossing two rules with two scenarios revealed that step-by-step reasoning avoids rule blindness, whereas fast detectors do not.
The Internal Compliance Score (ICS) provides a retraining-free activation readout calibrated from ten labeled pairs, evaluated via a single projection.
A bag-of-words model matches the pooled generalization of ICS, and an adaptive white-box attack eliminates the mechanical pass-rate gains achieved when using ICS to rank candidate responses.
summary.why_it_matters: Deployed AI compliance guards may offer a false sense of security by triggering on scenario context rather than actual regulatory rule violations.

security.title: Topological Attribution Distance (TAD): Revealing Segment-Level RAG Influence on LLM Output Geometry for Incident Log Analysis

summary.tldr: Topological Attribution Distance (TAD) uses segment-level ablation attribution and persistent geometry changes in the LLM's embedding space to identify which retrieved incident log segments most influence generated outputs.
key_points: Introduces Topological Attribution Distance (TAD) to measure the global geometric shape changes in model outputs relative to retrieved context.
Employs segment-level ablation attribution on cybersecurity incident logs to quantify evidence influence via changes in the embedding space.
Leverages the LLM's internal hidden states to provide adaptive, verifiable evidence tracing without relying solely on standard token attribution.
Addresses attribution failures caused by complex, highly similar evidence sources in cybersecurity and agentic AI decision chains.
summary.why_it_matters: TAD provides a mechanism for cybersecurity analysts to trace agentic AI decisions back to specific incident log segments, enabling reliable evidence verification and root-cause analysis.

security.title: What to Remember, What to Reveal: Privacy-Aware Memory for Conversational Agents

summary.tldr: SP-Mem is a privacy-aware memory architecture for conversational agents that decouples memory utility from exact private-value exposure across the full data life cycle.
key_points: Identifies and separates sensitive information, such as PII, directly from raw user inputs.
Stores sanitized contextual content and exact private values in isolated data structures.
Selectively retrieves exact private values only when required by the task and explicitly permitted by user consent.
Introduces a privacy-aware memory benchmark designed to jointly evaluate response quality, privacy protection behavior, and inference cost.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables long-term agent personalization while minimizing unnecessary storage and exposure of sensitive user data.

security.title: DSPrompt: Dynamic Soft Prompt Defense Against M-RAG Corruption

summary.tldr: DSPrompt uses a dynamic min-max trained soft prompt framework across frozen M-RAG encoder layers to defend against poisoning attacks without adding query-time overhead.
key_points: Inserts learnable soft prompts into every layer of frozen visual and textual encoders using a shallow-to-deep length schedule.
Employs dynamic min-max training where an online attacker crafts adversarial documents while the defender updates to eject them from top-k retrieval.
Preserves benign document ranking and diversity while adding less than 1% additional parameters.
Allows pre-computation and indexing of the defended encoder, avoiding per-query optimization or inference runtime penalties.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables robust defense against M-RAG embedding poisoning attacks at a fraction of the computational cost of existing query-time detection methods.

security.title: LLMs for Zero-Shot Threat Detection via Structured Risk Indicators

summary.tldr: A two-stage LLM framework combines chronological log timelines, RAG for historical user context, and structured risk indicators to improve zero-shot threat detection for insider threats and APTs.
key_points: The framework converts heterogeneous logs into user timelines, uses RAG for personalized historical context, generates structured risk indicators, and classifies them across temporal sequences.
Tested on CERT r5.2 (insider threats) and PicoDomain (APTs) using four configurations of two open-weight LLMs in retrieval and non-retrieval modes.
Outperformed the GABM baseline, boosting F1-scores by up to 11.40 percentage points on CERT r5.2 and 31.50 percentage points on PicoDomain.
Retrieval primary benefits weaker LLMs by producing more discriminative risk indicators, whereas stronger models achieve similar performance without RAG.
Indicator quality is the primary driver of zero-shot detection performance, with optimal stage-to-model assignments varying by dataset.
summary.why_it_matters: Generating intermediate structured risk indicators enables LLMs to detect complex cyber attacks across long temporal windows without requiring domain-specific training data.

security.title: Proving the Utility of Large Language Models in Cybersecurity Simulations: A Comprehensive Examination

summary.tldr: Integrating Large Language Models into cybersecurity simulations automates synthetic environment creation and achieves up to a 94.5% network compromise rate with a 25,000x to 50,000x execution speedup over traditional reinforcement learning.
key_points: Structured YAML formats represent complex network configurations for LLM-driven pipelines to aid reinforcement learning agent training.
LLM-instantiated Python agents outperform classical methods like Double Q-learning with Prioritized Experience Replay (PER) in efficiency, adaptability, and realism.
In empirical benchmarks on synthetic topologies, LLM agents reached a 94.5% compromise rate, taking 0.02-0.06 seconds per assessment.
summary.why_it_matters: LLMs can drastically reduce training time and resource overhead for cybersecurity simulations, allowing teams to test defenses against realistic, rapidly deployed attack vectors.

security.title: Security Assessment of DeepSeek Harness with A.I.G: Evaluating Resistance to Indirect Prompt Injection

summary.tldr: Researchers evaluated DeepSeek Harness against indirect prompt injection using AI-Infra-Guard across 14,560 executions, identifying peak attack success rates of 25.5% for hidden Unicode and 17.0% for fake-completion attacks.
key_points: Evaluated 14,560 controlled executions covering 16 indirect-content channels, 35 payload objectives, and 12 attack methods using local fixtures for sensitive sinks.
Achieved peak attack success rates of 25.5% (RuleJudge) using hidden Unicode in file mode and 17.0% (LLMJudge) using fake-completion attacks in text mode.
Observed the highest channel-specific vulnerability in the file-mode skills channel, which reached a 16.0% success rate under RuleJudge.
Compared evaluation methodologies, finding LLMJudge assigned partial compliance more frequently than RuleJudge (7.3% versus 2.0%).
summary.why_it_matters: The findings demonstrate that agentic LLM harnesses remain vulnerable to indirect prompt injection through files and tool contexts, highlighting the need for defensive controls between untrusted content and sensitive actions.

security.title: CompoSkill: Compositional Skill Chain Attacks from Individually Scanner-Passing LLM Agent Skills

summary.tldr: CompoSkill demonstrates that autonomous AI agent skills that individually pass safety scanners can be chained to execute multi-step attack paths with high success rates.
key_points: CompoSkill evaluates attack paths using a white-box attacker that knows the victim skill pool and a black-box attacker that builds a Skill Composition Graph to search for implicit lure chains.
The framework was evaluated on CompoSkill-Bench, comprising 1,140 records across five threat categories and six scenarios on the OpenClaw and Nanobot agent platforms.
White-box and black-box settings achieved risk Chain Formation Rates (CFR) of up to 83.3% and 80.6% respectively, bypassing individual package scanners.
Analysis revealed a bridge-bonus-then-hop-decay pattern where bridge skills boost attack success, but Attack Success Rate (ASR) degrades when chains exceed three skill hops.
summary.why_it_matters: Single-skill safety certification is insufficient for securing AI agent ecosystems because security risks arise dynamically at the execution-path level rather than within individual packages.

security.title: Securing AI-Generated Code: A Just-in-Time Vulnerability Detection and Remediation Pipeline

summary.tldr: An automated security pipeline enriches AI code findings with MITRE ATT&CK and CWE contexts to remediate vulnerabilities across four Claude models, achieving up to a 69% reduction in static analyzer findings.
key_points: The evaluation framework tests 26 LLMSecEval prompts across 9 CWE categories using parallel static analysis (CodeQL, Bandit) and an LLM Code Validator.
Pipeline 2 (P2), which feeds static analyzer findings back to the validator alongside threat context enrichment, reduced security findings by 29% to 69%, outperforming context-only Pipeline 1 (P1).
Remediation introduced new security findings in 15% to 22% of cases, with roughly 70% of those churn events limited to a single new issue.
Sonnet 4.6 achieved the highest pass rate and lowest residual findings under P2 remediation, despite Opus 4.8 being the stronger standalone code generation model.
summary.why_it_matters: Combining traditional static analysis tool output with enriched LLM validation creates a more effective automated code remediation process than relying solely on LLM self-correction or base generation capability.

security.title: Coverage Is Not Containment: A Fundamental Limit of Admission-Time Defenses Against Coordinated Poisoning of Vector Retrieval

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrate that admission-time filters cannot distinguish coordinated vector poisoning from legitimate niche uploads, proving a fundamental limit that requires shifting defense to retrieval-time demand tracking.
key_points: Coordinated adversaries inject small sets of unremarkable documents (e.g., m=10) that form an attack cone surrounding a target query, capturing 10/10 top-k positions in BGE-large / BEIR.
End-to-end attacks on a BGE-large + HNSW + Qwen2.5-7B pipeline forced the generator to emit planted claims in 88% of target queries, up from 0% baseline.
Admission-time classifiers perform no better than chance, achieving only a 4.2% detection rate at a 1% false-positive rate because attack cones geometrically mimic legitimate niche content.
A retrieval-time detector observing query demand achieves a 100% detection rate at the same 1% false-positive rate.
summary.why_it_matters: Security teams cannot rely on ingestion-time or hub-filtering gates to secure RAG vector databases and must implement retrieval-time monitoring.

security.title: Proof-of-Execution Memory: Defending LLM Agents Against Forged-Reasoning Attacks by Verifying What Actually Happened

summary.tldr: Proof-of-Execution Memory (PoEM) defends LLM agents against forged-reasoning attacks by using an HMAC-chained ledger of executed actions to verify past safety steps without inspecting memory contents.
key_points: FARMA attacks insert fabricated memory entries to skip safety steps, achieving 98-100% success on GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini compared to 44% on Llama-3.1-8B.
SENTINEL's keyword defense is completely bypassed on the first attempt when an attacker uses an LLM to reword forged entries, while also causing a 33-50% false positive rate on legitimate operations.
PoEM maintains a separate, tamper-evident HMAC-chained ledger updated exclusively by the trusted action layer to confirm actual execution before allowing a step to be skipped.
PoEM reduced attack success rates to 0% across three models and three scenarios with microseconds of overhead and near-zero false positives (0% in 8/9 test cells, 1.7% in the ninth).
summary.why_it_matters: PoEM prevents malicious context injection from bypassing LLM safety checks by decoupling authorization from untrusted, manipulable agent memory.

security.title: When the Playbook Breaks: AI Incident Response for Systems That Don't Behave Like Anything Else

summary.tldr: Enterprise AI adoption lacks mature incident response playbooks for handling compromised generative AI systems, despite established procedures for traditional threats like ransomware.
key_points: Most enterprise AI security governance currently limits itself to inventory tracking, acceptable use policies, and use-case approval processes.
Traditional security incident playbooks (ransomware, email compromise, cloud account takeover) fail to address the unique failure modes of compromised AI tools.
summary.why_it_matters: Security teams cannot rely on legacy incident response frameworks to effectively mitigate risks when generative AI systems are compromised.

security.title: Conjunctive Poisoning in AI Supply-Chain Applications

summary.tldr: A new attack vectors AI deployment pipelines by combining benign prompt wrappers with crafted configuration metadata to deterministically modify post-generation behavior without altering model weights or training data.
key_points: Demonstrates a conjunctive-gate attack relying on wrapper markers and cryptographically bound JSON/YAML metadata across 15 open- and closed-source LLMs/VLMs.
Evaluates existing defenses, finding static metadata inspection, wrapper scanners, PromptShield, and SigStore artifact signing insufficient for this execution layer.
Introduces TIF-BAH, a lightweight middleware defense that verifies wrapper integrity and logs behavioral attestations during inference.
summary.why_it_matters: AI supply-chain security must expand beyond model weights and prompts to protect textual configuration metadata and wrapper artifacts from runtime behavioral manipulation.

security.title: Bounded Agents: Delegation Security for Multi-Agent AI Systems

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced the Agentic Principal Chain (APC), an authorization framework that tracks delegated authority, limits scopes and budgets, and enforces composition closure to prevent unauthorized multi-agent action combinations.
key_points: APC evaluates each request against session state using six authorization checks outside the model layer.
The framework proves Blast Radius Monotonicity and Composition Soundness under a complete restriction set with serialized admission.
In testing across 3,154 instances, APC reduced AgentDojo exfiltration from 75-100% to 0% and blocked all 544 InjecAgent data-stealing attempts.
Intent binding decreased task destruction from 38.6% to 4.0% and manipulation from 90.5% to 12.1%, with a 99th percentile authorization latency of 0.24 ms.
summary.why_it_matters: It shifts multi-agent security from prompt-level mitigations to deterministic authorization controls, preventing prompt injections from executing malicious actions even if the model is compromised.

security.title: Assessing Attack Surfaces in Generative Search Engines through Publisher Attributes: A Case Study in Political Domains

summary.tldr: A new evaluation framework introduces the content-injection barrier metric to characterize generative search engine (GSE) vulnerability to citation poisoning across political domains and user profiles.
key_points: Introduces the 'content-injection barrier' metric to quantify the difficulty of injecting arbitrary web content at specific publisher authority levels.
Evaluates citation selection and personalization vulnerability across three major GSEs using political domain data from the United States and Japan.
Finds that attack surfaces vary significantly by GSE model and underlying web search functionality, with ruling political parties exhibiting a broader attack surface than opposition parties.
Demonstrates that embedding user profiles for personalization has minimal impact on altering the GSE attack surface.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding citation preference and search engine mechanics helps defenders mitigate web content poisoning attacks aimed at manipulating LLM-generated search results.

security.title: Bit-Flip Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models: Action-Decoding Architecture Shapes the Vulnerability

summary.tldr: Researchers demonstrated the first targeted bit-flip attack on quantized Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, revealing that action-decoding architecture dictates vulnerability, with direct regression failing in 1-5 flips while flow-matching policies require ~100.
key_points: Gradient-selected bit-flips reduce closed-loop VLA success to 0%, whereas hundreds of random bit-flips cause no harm.
Model vulnerability depends on the action head: direct regression and token policies fail in 1-5 flips, while flow-matching policies require ~100-300 flips.
Applying a fixed-direction manifold-escape loss reduced Pi0's attack budget from ~1000 to ~100 flips.
Protecting just 5.3% of weights in a direct head model increased the open-loop failure threshold from 3 to 100 flips.
Real-robot validation confirmed task-calibrated emulated attacks resulted in 0/20 task successes, compared to 14/20 for clean models and 16/20 for global-random flips.
summary.why_it_matters: Hardware-level memory faults like Rowhammer pose a severe physical security risk to deployed embodied AI systems, making weight integrity a critical defense boundary.

infra.title: Developing Nemotron 3.5 Lightning NVFP4 with QAD Using NVIDIA Model Optimizer

summary.tldr: NVIDIA released the Nemotron 3.5 Lightning NVFP4 checkpoint, which uses Quantization-Aware Distortion to compress model size from 66 GB to 22 GB.
key_points: Uses NVFP4 quantization via the NVIDIA Model Optimizer.
Compresses the full-precision model checkpoint from 66 GB down to 22 GB.
Achieves up to 4x faster throughput while maintaining accuracy.
summary.why_it_matters: The 3x reduction in model size and 4x increase in throughput allow developers to run high-accuracy Nemotron models with significantly lower memory and compute requirements.

infra.title: Distributed Layerwise Offload: Scaling Toward 200B+ DiT Models Efficiently in vLLM-Omni

summary.tldr: vLLM-Omni introduced Distributed Layerwise Offload (DLO), a technique that shards and streams Diffusion Transformer (DiT) weights across devices to run large models like 124 GB Cosmos3-Super on 64 GB HBM devices.
key_points: Uses double-buffered prefetching to overlap Host-to-Device (H2D) transfers with AllGather weight reconstruction across devices.
Shards host memory usage so cgroup-visible host memory scales as O(model_size + dp_size × constant) instead of duplicating the full model per DP rank.
Supports a --dlo-no-use-allgather flag to disable weight sharding when AllGather synchronization overhead outweighs host memory savings.
Requires vLLM 0.27.0 with vLLM-Omni v0.27.0rc1, incorporating PR #5864 to enable independent request dispatch per DP rank.
summary.why_it_matters: DLO enables serving massive video and image diffusion models exceeding single-device HBM capacity without requiring prohibitive multi-copy host RAM allocation.

infra.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning now available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart

summary.tldr: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, enabling simplified deployment of an open, high-throughput model built for agentic workloads.
key_points: Features a hybrid Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture with 30B total parameters and 3B active parameters, supporting up to a 1M-token context window.
Utilizes DFlash speculative decoding to deliver up to 4x higher throughput and 30% faster task completion for agentic tool use.
Distilled from NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra and runnable on a single GPU in both BF16 and quantized NVFP4 formats.
Achieves benchmark scores such as 81.94 (BF16) / 81.62 (NVFP4) on MMLU Pro and 51.56 (BF16) / 52.80 (NVFP4) on SWE-bench Verified.
summary.why_it_matters: Developers can route high-volume, specialized agent steps to a smaller, single-GPU model, reducing cost and latency compared to using frontier-scale infrastructure for every task.

summary.tldr: OpenAI has published insights on how AI is reshaping cybersecurity for both attackers and defenders, along with recommendations for security teams.
key_points: AI technology is actively changing the threat landscape for both cyber attackers and defenders.
OpenAI is updating its internal operational security practices to mitigate AI-enabled threats.
Strategic guidance is provided for external security teams to strengthen defenses against evolving AI risks.
summary.why_it_matters: Security teams must adapt their operational defenses to counter the dual-use capabilities of AI as both threat actors and defenders adopt the technology.

vendors.title: New policy ideas for the Intelligence Age

summary.tldr: OpenAI has funded 14 independent policy research projects focused on expanding economic opportunity and enhancing societal resilience for the Intelligence Age.
key_points: OpenAI selected and funded 14 independent policy projects.
The initiative focuses on developing new AI policy ideas.
Target outcomes include expanding economic opportunity and strengthening societal resilience.
summary.why_it_matters: The funded projects aim to establish actionable public policy frameworks to address the economic and societal impacts of advancing AI technologies.

vendors.title: Qwen 3.8 27B scores 52 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index

summary.tldr: Qwen 3.8 27B achieved a score of 52 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, matching or nearly matching much larger competitive frontier models.
key_points: Qwen 3.8 27B scored 52 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.
The 27B parameter model tied the score of GPT-5.6 Luna (max).
It scored one point behind the 753B parameter GLM-5.2 (max) and the 1.6B parameter DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 (max).
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that a 27B parameter model can deliver benchmark performance competitive with significantly larger high-end models.

vendors.title: We Tracked a Shipment of Rare Books. It Ended at an Amazon AI Training Facility

summary.tldr: A 404 Media investigation used an Apple AirTag to track a 1,000-book marketplace purchase directly to an Amazon facility conducting destructive book scanning for AI training.
key_points: A bookseller placed an Apple AirTag inside a 1,000-book order placed on the Biblio marketplace by an anonymous, price-insensitive buyer.
The AirTag tracked the shipment to the VGT3 section of Amazon's LAS8 facility in northeast Las Vegas.
Amazon worker forum discussions confirmed that the VGT3 location performs high-volume destructive book scanning.
summary.why_it_matters: The tracking provides concrete evidence of large-scale physical book acquisition and destructive scanning operations by major tech companies to build AI training datasets.

summary.tldr: Doug Turnbull proposes assigning tags from large vocabularies to content by asking LLMs to generate freeform categories and matching those predictions to existing tags using vector embeddings.
key_points: Large tag sets (such as 1,856 tags) exceed reasonable prompt context limits for direct classification.
Prompting the model to generate hypothetical tags without showing it the existing vocabulary bypasses prompt size constraints.
Vector embeddings map the model's generated tags against the existing tag corpus to identify the closest concrete matches.
Prompts can include structural examples of desired classification shapes to guide the model's unconstrained output.
summary.why_it_matters: This technique allows systems to categorize content against massive, pre-existing taxonomies without exceeding context windows or degrading LLM classification accuracy.

vendors.title: How RingCentral builds AI-native work from engineering to ops

summary.tldr: RingCentral integrates ChatGPT Work and OpenAI Codex to accelerate its AI product development and centralize operational intelligence across engineering and operations teams.
key_points: Deploys ChatGPT Work to unify operational intelligence across engineering and ops departments.
Leverages OpenAI Codex to accelerate the development of AI-driven products.
summary.why_it_matters: Combining ChatGPT Work and Codex streamlines internal operations while speeding up the delivery of AI capabilities within RingCentral's product portfolio.
